senses.gloss:
कङ्क् कङ्क्, cl. 1. A. कङ्कते, -कितुम्, to
go; [cf. Hib. cichet, ‘walking;’ ciocair, ‘a
way, a road:’ Lith. kankù; ifs-kankù, ‘to come to.’]

कङ्क कङ्क, अस्, m. a heron (a bird of prey?);
a kind of mango; an epithet of Yama; N. of a
king; a Vṛṣṇi; a son of Ugra-sena, a son of Śūra;
[]
pl., N. of a people; a title of Yudhiṣṭhira (from his
assuming the disguise of a Brāhman before king
Virāṭa); a false or pretended Brāhman; a man of
the second or military tribe (perhaps a man of that
caste pretending to be a Brāhman); one of the
eighteen divisions of the continent; the brother of
Kaṃsa; (आ), f. a sort of sandal; scent of the lotus;
N. of a daughter of Ugra-sena and sister of Kaṅka.
—कङ्क-चित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. collected into a heap
resembling a heron.
—कङ्क-तुण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a
Rakṣas.
—कङ्क-त्रोट, अस्, or कङ्क-त्रोटि, इस्, m.
a kind of fish, commonly काङ्किला; Esox Kankila.
—कङ्क-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a heron's feather fixed on
an arrow; (अस्, आ, अम्), furnished with the feathers of
a heron; (अस्), m. an arrow furnished with heron's
feathers.
—कङ्कपत्त्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, furnished with
heron's feathers.
—कङ्क-पर्वन्, आ, m., N. of a
serpent.
—कङ्क-माला, f. a kind of musical instru-
ment; beating time by clapping the hands.
—कङ्क-
मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, shaped like a heron's mouth;
(अस्, अम्), m. n. a pair of tongs, a sort of forceps.
—कङ्क-शत्रु, उस्, m. the plant Desmodium
Gangeticum.
—कङ्क-शाय, अस्, m. a dog (sleeping
like a heron).

कङ्कट कङ्कट or कङ्कटक, अस्, m. (said
to be fr. rt. कङ्क्), mail, defensive armour; an iron
hook to goad an elephant.
कङ्कटेरी कङ्कटेरी, f. turmeric.

कङ्कण कङ्कण, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be
fr. rt. कै), a bracelet, an ornament of the wrist
(used also as a weapon); a string or ribbon tied
round the wrist; an ornament round the foot of an
elephant; any ornament or trinket; a crest; (ई), f.
a small bell or tinkling ornament; an ornament
furnished with bells: see किङ्किणी; [cf. Lith. kan-
kala-s.]
—कङ्कण-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town,
called from कङ्कण-वर्ष.
—कङ्कण-प्रिय,
अस्, m., N. of a servant of Śiva.
—कङ्कण-भू-
षण, अस्, आ, अम्, adorned with tinkling orna-
ments.
—कङ्कण-मणी, f. the jewel in a bracelet.
—कङ्कण-वर्ष, अस्, m., N. of an alchemist^1;
epithet of the king Kṣemagupta.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210422. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/60.
कङ्कणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, ornamented with a bracelet.

कङ्कणीका, f. an ornament furnished with bells;
a string tied round the wrist.

कङ्कत कङ्कत, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. or कङ्क-
तिका, f. a comb, a hair-comb; (अस्), m. a tree; (accord-
ing to Sāy.) a poisonous animal, a slightly venomous
reptile (mentioned in a verse of Ṛg-veda 1. 191,
used as a mystical spell against poison).
कङ्कतीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family.

कङ्कर कङ्कर, अस्, ई, अम्, vile, bad; (अम्),
n. buttermilk mixed with water; a high number, =
100 niyutas.

कङ्करोल कङ्करोल, अस्, m. the plant Alan-
gium Hexapetalum. See निकोचक.

कङ्कलोड्य कङ्कलोड्य, अम्, n. a kind of
drug, = अल्कलोड्य.

कङ्काल कङ्काल, अस्, अम्, m. n. a skeleton;
[cf. Mod. Gr. κώκαλον.]
—कङ्काल-केतु, उस्, m.,
N. of a Dānava.
—कङ्काल-भैरव-तन्त्र, अम्,
n., N. of a Tantra.
—कङ्कालमालिन्, ई, m. an epi-
thet of Śiva, whose necklace is formed of bones.

कङ्कालय कङ्कालय or कल्कालय, अस्, m.,
N. of an author.

कङ्कु कङ्कु, उस्, m. = कङ्गु, N. of a son
of Ugra-sena and brother of Kaṃsa.

कङ्कुष्ठ कङ्कुष्ठ, अस्, m. a medicinal earth,
described as of two colours, one of a silvery and one
of a gold colour, or one of a light and one of a dark
yellow.
कङ्कूष कङ्कूष, (?) Atharva-veda IX. 8, 2.
कङ्केरु कङ्केरु, उस्, m. a kind of crow.

कङ्केल्ल कङ्केल्ल, अस्, m. the tree Jonesia
Aśoka; a kind of pot-herb, Chenopodium Esculentum.
कङ्केल्लि, इस्, m. Jonesia Aśoka.

कङ्कोल कङ्कोल, अस्, m. a king of the Nāgas;
N. of the author of a hymn called Gaṇapatyārādhana.

कङ्ख कङ्ख, अम्, n. enjoyment, fruition;
(perhaps a combination of क and ख.)

कङ्गु कङ्गु, उस्, f. or कङ्गुनी, f. a kind of
Panic seed, Panicum Italicum; several varieties of it
are cultivated and form articles of food for the poor.
—कङ्गुनी-पत्त्रा, f. a kind of grass, = पण्यान्धा.

कङ्गुल कङ्गुल, अस्, m. the hand; [cf.
अङ्गुलि.]

काङ्कायन काङ्कायन, अस्, m. (a patronymic
fr. कङ्क), N. of a Muni.

काङ्क्ष् काङ्क्ष्, cl. 1. P. काङ्क्षति, च-
काङ्क्ष, ep. also A. काङ्क्षते, &c.,
काङ्क्षितुम्, to wish, desire; to strive to obtain;
to long for, hope for (with acc.), expect; to wait; to
look for anything (with dat.): Caus. काङ्क्षयति,
अचकाङ्क्षत्: Desid. चिकाङ्क्षिषति: Intens. चा-
काङ्क्ष्यते and चाकांष्टि; [cf. Hib. cachta,
‘hunger;’ Goth. huhru-s, ‘hunger;’ hungrja, ‘to
be hungry;’ Germ. Hunger.]

काङ्क्षत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, or काङ्क्षमाण, अस्,
आ, अम्, wishing, desiring, hoping, expecting.
काङ्क्षा, f. wish, inclination, desire.

काङ्क्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, wished, desired; expected,
longed for; (अम्), n. wish, desire.

काङ्क्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, desiring, expecting, longing for
(with acc. or at the end of a compound).
—काङ्क्षि-
ता, f. wish, desire.

काङ्क्षोरु काङ्क्षोरु, उस्, m. a heron; also
written काङ्क्षारु.
काङ्गा काङ्गा, f., N. of a plant, Orris root.
काङ्गुक काङ्गुक, अम्, n. a kind of corn.
